en.greeting: Hi! Today you take your stories, your rhetoric and your voice onto a stage: a keynote built on one big idea, devices that work for the ear, and reading the room as you speak. One honest note: the recordings are one plain voice, so the pauses and stresses are written in the notes. Say every line out loud.

steps.title: One big idea, one clear shape
steps.text: Quick recap: you have hooks and stories (C1), devices on the page (Rhetoric & Persuasion) and a voice that fits the room (Natural Prosody). Now: the keynote.
steps.body:
A **keynote** is built on **one big idea**: one sentence the audience can repeat at home. Cut whatever doesn't serve it.
- **A shape for 15–20 minutes:** hook (about 1 min) → the idea in one sentence → **three parts**, each a point + a story or evidence → **the close**.
- **The close returns to the opening** (a **callback**): the same story or image, now changed, then the idea and *Thank you.* No new material at the end.
**The trap:** a long protocol greeting (*Yang terhormat …*) and *Sekian, terima kasih* waste your best minutes. One line: *Good morning, everyone.*

steps.title: Close the circle
steps.text: Pak Hasan is giving the graduation speech at the university in Yogyakarta where he studied.

options: Before I finish, here are three more tips for your careers, and a story from my years in Singapore.
That's all from me. Thank you for listening, and congratulations once again.
Twenty-eight years ago, I stood at that gate holding a map upside down. Today, you hold yours the right way up. Go and use it.
question.prompt: He opened with his first day on this campus in 1998: lost at the main gate, holding a campus map upside down. Which closing calls back to the opening?
question.explanation: The third closing returns to the **opening image** (the gate, the upside-down map) and shows what has changed: a **callback** that ends on the idea. The first adds **new material** at the very end. The second is the flat *That's all* ending, with nothing for the audience to take home.

steps.title: Built for the ear
steps.text: A reader can re-read a sentence. A listener can't, so a talk needs help a text doesn't.
steps.body:
- **Preview** the map: *I'll tell you three stories.*
- **Signpost** every turn: *Now, the second story.*
- **Recap**, and **repeat the key line** word for word two or three times.
**Write for the ear:** short sentences (one idea each), concrete words (*forty orders*, not *a significant increase*), **active voice** (*Our drivers delivered it*, not *It was delivered by our drivers*), and talk to the audience with *you* and questions.
**The trap:** a *naskah pidato* full of passives (*telah dilaksanakan* → *has been carried out*) is correct but heavy to hear.

steps.title: Turn to the audience
steps.text: Sari has just finished her opening story at a startup summit in Jakarta. Now she turns the story towards the audience with a short question.

question.solution: So what does this mean for you?
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Jadi, apa artinya ini bagi Anda?
question.explanation: **So what does this mean for you?** is short, uses *you* and moves the talk from her story to the listeners: a spoken signpost. Question order: *what* + *does* + *this* + *mean*.

steps.title: Rhetoric for the ear
steps.text: You know these devices from the page. Spoken, timing does half the work.
steps.body:
Notation: CAPITALS = stress · | = pause · || = long pause (the app's voice can't do these: say them yourself).
- **Rule of three:** short, same shape, a pause before the third, fall ↘ on it.
- **Anaphora:** the same opening each time; stress what changes.
- **Rhetorical question:** ask, then **stop** for 2–3 seconds.
- **Power pause** before the key word: *…was || trust.*
- **Contrast pair:** stress both opposites.
- **Callback:** an image from the opening returns.
**Delivery:** eye contact for a whole sentence, move on transitions, stand still for the key line, vary your voice. Key moments only.

steps.title: Say it aloud
steps.text: Tap each line. The recording is plain; the note shows where to pause and what to stress. Then say it yourself, with the timing.
steps.body: Notice how the last line answers the first: that's a callback. In a real talk there would be fifteen minutes between them.

steps.title: Listen: a TEDx-style talk
steps.text: Dimas is giving a TEDx-style talk in Bandung about learning after university. Press play.

question.listen: A degree does not prove what you know. It proves that you can keep learning.
options: the rule of three
a contrast pair (antithesis)
a callback to the opening
question.prompt: Listen to one line from his talk. Which device does it use?
question.explanation: Two opposite ideas in a balanced pair, what a degree does **not** prove and what it **does** prove: a **contrast pair** (antithesis). Spoken, he'd stress KNOW and LEARNing, with a pause | between the sentences. There are only two parts, not three, and nothing returns from an opening.

steps.title: Read the room
steps.text: Last part: watch your audience while you speak, and adapt. A keynote is a plan, not a script.
steps.body:
- **Puzzled faces, whispering** → plain words + an example: *Let me put that another way.*
- **Phones out, restless** → cut the section short, go to a story, or ask a show of hands.
- **Leaning forward at the back** → speak up, speak to the back row.
- **'Could you repeat that?'** → slow down, repeat the number.
- **Laughter, nodding** → it's working: let it land.
- **Silence after 'Any questions?'** → often shyness (*sungkan*): give them a moment.
- **Running late** → cut calmly: *In the interest of time, …* Never speed up.
- **A joke falls flat** → don't explain it, don't keep apologising: smile and move on.

steps.title: Puzzled faces
steps.text: Dr. Wulan is speaking at a TEDx-style evening in Bandung about clean water.

options: Repeat the same sentence, more slowly and more loudly.
Carry on with the script: they can look the term up after the talk.
Say it in plain words with a quick example: 'In other words, clean water the city produces but never sells, mostly because it leaks from old pipes.'
question.prompt: She says: 'This is a classic case of non-revenue water.' Many faces look puzzled, and two people whisper to each other. What's the best move?
question.explanation: Puzzled faces after a technical term mean the audience has lost her, so she **says it again in plain words with an example**. Repeating the same jargon more slowly and loudly doesn't make it clearer, and carrying on loses the room for the rest of the section.

steps.title: When the joke falls flat
steps.text: Budi, the founder of a logistics startup, opens his keynote at a startup summit in Jakarta with a joke about investors.

options: Smile, say 'OK, I'll stick to logistics', and move straight on to his opening story.
Explain the joke, so that the audience understands why it was funny.
Apologise several times: 'Sorry, sorry, that was a bad joke, I'm really not funny.'
question.prompt: Silence. Nobody laughs. What should he do?
question.explanation: **Smile, one light line, move on**: if he doesn't make it a big moment, the audience forgets it in seconds. Explaining a joke never makes it funny, and apologising again and again makes everyone uncomfortable and costs him the confident start.

steps.title: Watch real speakers
steps.text: Two TED talks with real voices: why a talk needs one idea, and how pace, pitch, volume and silence work. Watch them for the pauses the app's voice can't make.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini cerita, retorika dan suaramu kamu bawa ke atas panggung: keynote yang dibangun di atas satu gagasan besar, gaya bahasa yang bekerja untuk telinga, dan membaca suasana selagi kamu bicara. Catatan jujur: rekamannya satu suara biasa, jadi jeda dan tekanan ditulis di catatan. Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan suara keras.

steps.title: Satu gagasan besar, satu bentuk yang jelas
steps.text: Kilas balik singkat: kamu sudah punya hook dan cerita (C1), gaya bahasa di atas kertas (Rhetoric & Persuasion) dan suara yang cocok dengan ruangan (Natural Prosody). Sekarang: keynote.
steps.body:
**Keynote** dibangun di atas **satu gagasan besar**: satu kalimat yang bisa diulang audiens di rumah. Buang apa pun yang tidak mendukungnya.
- **Bentuk untuk 15–20 menit:** hook (sekitar 1 menit) → gagasan dalam satu kalimat → **tiga bagian**, masing-masing poin + cerita atau bukti → **penutup**.
- **Penutup kembali ke pembukaan** (**callback**): cerita atau gambaran yang sama, yang kini sudah berubah, lalu gagasannya dan *Thank you.* Tidak ada materi baru di akhir.
**Jebakannya:** salam protokoler yang panjang (*Yang terhormat …*) dan *Sekian, terima kasih* menghabiskan menit-menit terbaikmu. Satu baris saja: *Good morning, everyone.*

steps.title: Tutup lingkarannya
steps.text: Pak Hasan menyampaikan pidato wisuda di universitas di Yogyakarta tempat dia dulu kuliah.

options: Before I finish, here are three more tips for your careers, and a story from my years in Singapore.
That's all from me. Thank you for listening, and congratulations once again.
Twenty-eight years ago, I stood at that gate holding a map upside down. Today, you hold yours the right way up. Go and use it.
question.prompt: Dia membuka dengan hari pertamanya di kampus ini pada 1998: tersesat di gerbang utama, memegang peta kampus terbalik. Penutup mana yang kembali ke pembukaan (callback)?
question.explanation: Penutup ketiga kembali ke **gambaran pembuka** (gerbang, peta yang terbalik) dan menunjukkan apa yang sudah berubah: sebuah **callback** yang diakhiri dengan gagasannya. Penutup pertama menambah **materi baru** tepat di akhir. Penutup kedua adalah akhir datar *That's all*, tanpa apa pun untuk dibawa pulang audiens.

steps.title: Dibuat untuk telinga
steps.text: Pembaca bisa membaca ulang sebuah kalimat. Pendengar tidak bisa, jadi pidato butuh bantuan yang tidak dibutuhkan tulisan.
steps.body:
- **Preview** peta pidatomu: *I'll tell you three stories.*
- **Signpost** setiap perpindahan: *Now, the second story.*
- **Recap**, dan **ulangi kalimat kunci** kata per kata dua atau tiga kali.
**Tulis untuk didengar:** kalimat pendek (satu gagasan per kalimat), kata yang konkret (*forty orders*, bukan *a significant increase*), **kalimat aktif** (*Our drivers delivered it*, bukan *It was delivered by our drivers*), dan ajak audiens bicara dengan *you* dan pertanyaan.
**Jebakannya:** *naskah pidato* yang penuh kalimat pasif (*telah dilaksanakan* → *has been carried out*) memang benar, tapi berat didengar.

steps.title: Arahkan ke audiens
steps.text: Sari baru saja menyelesaikan cerita pembukanya di sebuah startup summit di Jakarta. Sekarang dia mengarahkan ceritanya ke audiens dengan sebuah pertanyaan singkat.

question.solution: So what does this mean for you?
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Jadi, apa artinya ini bagi Anda?
question.explanation: **So what does this mean for you?** pendek, memakai *you*, dan memindahkan pidato dari ceritanya ke para pendengar: sebuah penanda arah lisan. Urutan kata tanya: *what* + *does* + *this* + *mean*.

steps.title: Retorika untuk telinga
steps.text: Gaya bahasa ini sudah kamu kenal dari tulisan. Saat diucapkan, waktu yang tepat melakukan separuh pekerjaan.
steps.body:
Notasi: HURUF BESAR = tekanan · | = jeda · || = jeda panjang (suara aplikasi tidak bisa membuatnya: ucapkan sendiri).
- **Rule of three:** pendek, bentuk sama, jeda sebelum yang ketiga, nada turun ↘ di situ.
- **Anafora:** pembuka yang sama setiap kali; tekan bagian yang berubah.
- **Pertanyaan retoris:** tanyakan, lalu **diam** 2–3 detik.
- **Power pause** sebelum kata kunci: *…was || trust.*
- **Pasangan kontras:** tekan kedua kata yang berlawanan.
- **Callback:** gambaran dari pembukaan muncul lagi.
**Cara membawakan:** kontak mata selama satu kalimat penuh, bergerak saat pindah bagian, diam saat kalimat kunci, suara yang bervariasi. Hanya di saat penting.

steps.title: Ucapkan dengan suara keras
steps.text: Ketuk setiap kalimat. Rekamannya polos; catatannya menunjukkan di mana berhenti dan kata mana yang ditekan. Lalu ucapkan sendiri, dengan jedanya.
steps.body: Perhatikan bagaimana kalimat terakhir menjawab kalimat pertama: itulah callback. Dalam pidato sungguhan, ada lima belas menit di antara keduanya.

steps.title: Dengarkan: pidato bergaya TEDx
steps.text: Dimas menyampaikan pidato bergaya TEDx di Bandung tentang belajar setelah lulus kuliah. Tekan putar.

question.listen: A degree does not prove what you know. It proves that you can keep learning.
options: the rule of three
a contrast pair (antithesis)
a callback to the opening
question.prompt: Dengarkan satu kalimat dari pidatonya. Gaya bahasa apa yang dipakainya?
question.explanation: Dua gagasan berlawanan dalam pasangan yang seimbang, apa yang **tidak** dibuktikan oleh gelar dan apa yang **justru** dibuktikannya: **pasangan kontras** (antitesis). Saat diucapkan, dia akan menekan KNOW dan LEARNing, dengan jeda | di antara kedua kalimat. Hanya ada dua bagian, bukan tiga, dan tidak ada yang kembali dari pembukaan.

steps.title: Membaca suasana
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: perhatikan audiensmu selagi bicara, lalu sesuaikan. Keynote adalah rencana, bukan naskah.
steps.body:
- **Wajah bingung, berbisik** → kata-kata sederhana + contoh: *Let me put that another way.*
- **Ponsel keluar, gelisah** → persingkat bagian itu, pindah ke cerita, atau minta angkat tangan.
- **Yang di belakang mencondongkan badan** → bicara lebih keras, arahkan ke barisan belakang.
- **'Could you repeat that?'** → pelankan tempo, ulangi angkanya.
- **Tawa, anggukan** → berhasil: biarkan meresap.
- **Hening setelah 'Any questions?'** → sering karena sungkan: beri waktu sebentar.
- **Waktu hampir habis** → potong dengan tenang: *In the interest of time, …* Jangan bicara lebih cepat.
- **Lelucon garing** → jangan dijelaskan, jangan minta maaf terus: tersenyum dan lanjutkan.

steps.title: Wajah-wajah bingung
steps.text: Dr. Wulan berbicara di sebuah malam bergaya TEDx di Bandung tentang air bersih.

options: Repeat the same sentence, more slowly and more loudly.
Carry on with the script: they can look the term up after the talk.
Say it in plain words with a quick example: 'In other words, clean water the city produces but never sells, mostly because it leaks from old pipes.'
question.prompt: Dia berkata: 'This is a classic case of non-revenue water.' Banyak wajah terlihat bingung, dan dua orang saling berbisik. Apa langkah terbaik?
question.explanation: Wajah bingung setelah istilah teknis berarti audiens tertinggal, jadi dia **mengulanginya dengan kata-kata sederhana dan contoh**. Mengulang istilah yang sama dengan lebih pelan dan lebih keras tidak membuatnya lebih jelas, dan meneruskan naskah membuat ruangan tertinggal sampai akhir bagian itu.
displayOptions: Ulangi kalimat yang sama lebih lambat dan lebih keras.
Lanjutkan naskah: audiens bisa mencari istilahnya nanti.
Jelaskan dengan contoh singkat: 'In other words, clean water the city produces but never sells, mostly because it leaks from old pipes.'

steps.title: Saat lelucon garing
steps.text: Budi, pendiri sebuah startup logistik, membuka keynote-nya di sebuah startup summit di Jakarta dengan lelucon tentang investor.

options: Smile, say 'OK, I'll stick to logistics', and move straight on to his opening story.
Explain the joke, so that the audience understands why it was funny.
Apologise several times: 'Sorry, sorry, that was a bad joke, I'm really not funny.'
question.prompt: Hening. Tidak ada yang tertawa. Apa yang sebaiknya dia lakukan?
question.explanation: **Tersenyum, satu kalimat ringan, lanjutkan**: kalau dia tidak membesar-besarkannya, audiens melupakannya dalam beberapa detik. Menjelaskan lelucon tidak pernah membuatnya lucu, dan minta maaf berulang-ulang membuat semua orang canggung dan menghilangkan pembukaan yang percaya diri.
displayOptions: Tersenyum, bilang 'OK, I'll stick to logistics', lalu lanjut ke cerita pembuka.
Jelaskan leluconnya agar audiens mengerti mengapa itu lucu.
Minta maaf berkali-kali: 'Sorry, sorry, that was a bad joke, I'm really not funny.'

steps.title: Tonton pembicara sungguhan
steps.text: Dua pidato TED dengan suara asli: kenapa pidato butuh satu gagasan, dan bagaimana tempo, nada, volume dan keheningan bekerja. Tonton untuk mendengar jeda yang tidak bisa dibuat oleh suara aplikasi.
